supportable_proposition: 19 municipal procurement/AI-governance employees in seven U.S. cities interviewed
strict_inference_boundary: A documented qualitative sample; not a nationally representative survey; respondents and cities intentionally anonymized.

supportable_proposition: Interviewees describe vendors withholding models, disaggregated performance and training data requested by cities
strict_inference_boundary: No named signed contract clauses or independently corroborated breach in these anonymized accounts.

supportable_proposition: One city department monitored an already procured gunshot detection AI system using locally devised metrics after vendor did not supply evaluations
strict_inference_boundary: This supports reported municipal monitoring, not independent audit logs or proof of causal remedy efficacy.

supportable_proposition: AI drone vendor disclosed deployment limitations and a city adjusted its usage policy accordingly
strict_inference_boundary: No specific signed audit or contractual enforcement action; do not infer formal remedy or supplier sanction.

supportable_proposition: Interviewees describe a city declining AI acquisition after a provider treated performance evidence as proprietary
strict_inference_boundary: A prospective acquisition was rejected; this is not post-award contract monitoring.

supportable_proposition: Interviewees mention a city stopped paying for a purchased service because of unwanted generative-AI note-taking features
strict_inference_boundary: A participant account of purchase stopping does not establish breach, legal termination right, sanctions or vendor correction.

supportable_proposition: Some AI features were introduced under existing vendor contracts through scope expansion and alternate purchase pathways
strict_inference_boundary: Do not infer prevalence of this practice across all governments from 19 nonprobability interviews.

supportable_proposition: Normative public law framework argues for traceable audit rights, supplier telemetry and operational ability to contest outsourced AI decisions
strict_inference_boundary: Paper proposes what ought to be contracted; it does not show clauses signed or activated in an observed government purchase.

supportable_proposition: SmartHS deployed for social-insurance services in three Chinese cities with operational case counts
strict_inference_boundary: Service-contract procurement, external supplier and audit/remediation rights are not established by accessible abstract.

supportable_proposition: Buenos Aires government helpline call audit uses locally deployed open-source speech recognition and LLM classifiers
strict_inference_boundary: Government AI use is not automatically external AI procurement; print year 2026 but online publication October 2025.

supportable_proposition: Framework for deciding which public-sector AI categories suit accountability constraints
strict_inference_boundary: Framework is not proof of signed AI procurement or any exercised contractual right.

supportable_proposition: Researchers applied data-mining algorithms to Ecuador public tender evaluation records to identify possible irregularities
strict_inference_boundary: AI deployed by the research team is not a demonstrated AI system purchased by a government buyer.

supportable_proposition: Algorithmic Equity Toolkit gives advocates questions to ask vendors and public officials about algorithmic technology
strict_inference_boundary: The toolkit is not evidence of an actual government procurement contract or vendor remedy.
